A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoNVS and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original NVS benchmark results, geometric evaluations, component ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds refinement, guidance-scale, gating-uncertainty, and memory analyses.

M1.justification: The reported architecture removes the separate projection MLP between RefineNet and feature fusion: v2 directly fuses refined features in Section 3.2, Figure 3, and Eqs. (7)–(8). The main lifting, refinement, adaptive fusion, and training objectives remain.

E1.justification: The nine benchmarks and existing NVS tasks remain. Figure 4 adds a focused diagnostic on three reflective scenes: Garden Spheres, Toy Car, and Sedan. Appendix B's change from eight to nine benchmarks corrects the already existing list rather than adding a dataset.

E2.justification: The external comparator methods and their retained benchmark participation are unchanged. The additional SSIM/LPIPS panels in Table 1 reproduce selected comparisons already present in Appendix Table 11. Difix3D+ becoming Difix3D in Table 12 is a naming correction.

E3.justification: New protocols include per-scene latent-reconstruction tests on 540 randomly sampled DL3DV test scenes with 3, 6, or 9 inputs, and a CFG-scale sweep on 10 DL3DV scenes. Peak GPU memory is also measured. Existing training settings and benchmark protocols remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Table 7 isolates RefineNet's contribution, Appendix C.3 tests reconstruction with and without refinement, C.4 tests CFG sensitivity, and Figure 8 adds memory analysis. Quantitative gate–uncertainty analysis replaces v1's temporal gate visualization, and Figure 10 adds blur case studies.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 and Figure 4 introduce Pearson-correlation estimates between absolute gate weights and geometry uncertainty across three scenes and denoising stages; v1's gate analysis was qualitative. Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Substantial new diagnostic results cover refinement, CFG sensitivity, gating, memory, and failure examples. Appendix C.3 reports nine-view reconstruction PSNR of 17.38 without refinement versus 18.75 with it; Figure 8 adds peak-memory measurements of 18.03 GB unpruned and 12.93 GB pruned. Retained benchmark scores, including Appendix Tables 11–13, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal fusion mapping in Eqs. (7)–(8) changes from projected refined features to refined features directly, and Table 10 removes the separate projection definition. Other splatting, feature-lifting, positional-encoding, and loss mathematics remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: feature-space geometry guidance, plug-and-play compatibility, improved geometry and camera control, and the same headline benchmark gains. New analyses support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets gating through measured geometry uncertainty and explains refinement as compensating for mismatches between opacity-based compositing and latent features. It also attributes fine-detail blur to feature-lifting information loss. v1 already discussed occlusion-related blur in Appendix H, so the general blur limitation is not wholly new.

D1.justification: New Figure 16 explicitly documents training-only target-view use for point-cloud construction, approximately 300-image source videos, and an InstantSplat step taking under one minute. The project-page link destination changes. These are documentation/access changes, without evidence that the retained training procedure was rerun.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.3 adds a focused critique of transferring earlier feature-splatting approaches to image synthesis, discussing latent additivity and contrasting NVS with discrete downstream tasks. The cited-work set remains unchanged; SEVA's arXiv-to-ICCV reference update is bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify fusion and co-visibility masking, Section 4.3 becomes 'Perceptual Quality,' Appendix C is revised and extended, and acknowledgements are added. Terminology and notation receive corrections, while the overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands into three metric panels using existing appendix results. Figure 3 is redrawn, Figure 4 gains uncertainty panels, and new displays cover memory, refinement, CFG sensitivity, preprocessing, and blur. The former temporal gate figure is removed. These substantive display changes extend beyond relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The RefineNet controls and CFG study strengthen support for the existing design, while memory measurements, preprocessing disclosure, and blur examples improve transparency. These targeted benefits outweigh losing the earlier temporal gate visualization. The principal benchmark evidence and overall scientific claims remain unchanged.
